definitions.explanation: The first child born to a couple. A somewhat literary or traditional term.

examples.japanese: {初子|ういご}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{生|う}まれた→生まれる：00905_umareru⟧。
{初子|ういご}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{名前|なまえ}→名前：02234_namae⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{決|き}める→決める：00858_kimeru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{時間|じかん}→時間：00468_jikan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦かかった→かかる：00711_kakaru⟧。
examples.english: It took time to decide the name for our firstborn.

examples.japanese: {初子|ういご}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{両親|りょうしん}→両親：00806_ryoushin⟧⟦にとって→にとって：06803_nitotte⟧⟦{特別|とくべつ}→特別：01120_tokubetsu⟧な⟦{存在|そんざい}→存在：03326_sonzai⟧だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: It is said that the firstborn child is a special existence for parents.

notes:
Composed of {初|うい} (first, initial) + {子|ご} (child). A classical reading — the more common modern equivalent is {第一子|だいいっし} or ⟦{最初|さいしょ}→最初：00882_saisho⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{子|こ}→子：09851_ko⟧. Also sometimes written as {初|うい}{児|ご}.

USAGE:
- Somewhat literary and traditional; found in formal writing, historical texts, and family-related contexts
- In everyday conversation, {第一子|だいいっし} or {一人目|ひとりめ}の{子|こ} is more common
- Can also be read as はつご, though ういご is the primary reading

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {初子|ういご}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{生|う}まれる→生まれる：00905_umareru⟧: a first child is born
- ⟦{待望|たいぼう}→待望：12545_taibou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{初子|ういご}: a long-awaited firstborn
- {初子|ういご}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{授|さず}かる→授かる：12797_sazukaru⟧: to be blessed with a first child

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{長男|ちょうなん}→長男：14519_chounan⟧: eldest son — specifically male
- ⟦{長女|ちょうじょ}→長女：14518_choujo⟧: eldest daughter — specifically female
- {第一子|だいいっし}: first child — the modern formal equivalent
- ⟦{末っ子|すえっこ}→末っ子：15132_suekko⟧: youngest child — the opposite position in birth order
